title: Orchestrated credential fabric and compact pullstream API (py/ts/go) + cross-sdk version bumps
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: multiple SDK teams requested a small, predictable surface for credential handoff and a compact pullstream-friendly streaming facade that is consistent across Python, TypeScript, and Go. This PR introduces a lightweight "credential fabric" (orchestrated credential wrappers + fallback registry) and a compact PullStreamAdapter across SDKs to improve ergonomics for streaming consumers, smooth credential rotation, and reduce duplication in app code. Work covers three SDK packages and a central internal crate used for shared protocol types. Summary of changes: 1) Credential fabric: introduces CredentialRegistry (language-specific API names: CredentialRegistry / CredFabric) and a CredentialChain composable that accepts multiple providers (static tokens, delegated channels, rotating leases). It exposes a small lifecycle: acquire(), refresh_hint(), and release() to make lease semantics explicit for streaming sessions. 2) PullStreamAdapter: a minimal streaming facade that normalizes chunk buffering, backpressure hints and reauth callbacks; it intentionally avoids heavyweight session objects so callers can easily await chunks in tight loops. 3) Retry presets: adds an "sdk:streaming-compact" retry profile that defaults to lower backoff jitter for short-lived streams and a conservative retry window for credential-refresh scenarios. 4) Cross-sdk parity: brings the same API names and idioms to Python, TypeScript and Go with shims to preserve backwards compatibility. 5) Version bumps: py-sdk -> 0.11.0, ts-sdk -> 2.4.1, go-sdk -> v1.8.0. Migration notes / compatibility: - Python: introduces redwood.session.CredentialRegistry and redwood.stream.PullStreamAdapter. Existing SessionManager remains; a compatibility shim SessionManager.migrate_to_registry() is provided to ease rollouts. - TypeScript: adds CredFabric and pullstream.light() convenience factory. Old streaming constructors still supported but marked deprecated with console warnings. - Go: renames SessionHandle->SessionHandleV2 in public surface and provides SessionHandle (thin wrapper) for compatibility during the deprecation window. Tests and runtime: comprehensive unit tests added across SDKs including new integration tests that simulate token rotation during active streaming and ensure no dropped chunks or double-invocation of auth hooks. Performance: minor overhead for the registry path on cold start (~0.8ms median) but steady-state throughput unchanged. Rollout plan: library level releases were coordinated; feature gate in the hosted API will toggle registry-backed delegation for enterprise customers first, then default for all in 2 weeks. Commits and rationale: - feat(cred): introduce credential fabric and registry with composable chain - feat(stream): add compact PullStreamAdapter and stream retry preset - refactor(py/ts/go): centralize token exchange infra into shared-types crate - test: add rotation/integration tests and CI matrix - docs: add migration guide and quickstart examples Known limitations and followups: - The Go wrapper increases binary size slightly due to shim layers; follow-up PR will peel shared helper to a submodule. - There are a couple of non-blocking lint warnings in ts examples that were deferred to a docs cleanup PR. Full description ends here.
